claims.text: Calculation settings
Max Amount, Lynx Reference Amount and Crop Coefficient.
claims.note: The full labels are "Daily Max Amount ({{unitsAbbr}})", "Lynx Reference Amount ({{unitsAbbr}})" and "Crop Coefficient (%)" (en-us.json:422, :420, :389). The tile shortens the first to "Max Amount".

claims.text: Three numbers decide every suggestion on the course: the daily maximum, the Lynx reference amount, and the crop coefficient.

evidence.ref: docs/claims/calculations.md §2.2 The chain, per station, per day

claims.note: These are the three site-wide inputs to Option 2, the production default. Each station's target, measured or modelled VWC, soil factor and today's ET also enter (SpatialAdjustService.cs:3031-3043). Under Option 1 none of the three is used and all three fields are disabled (sa-algorithm.service.ts:58-60; sa-settings-dlg.component.html:85, :100, :115).

claims.text: These are site-level settings — they apply to every user on the site.

claims.text: Changing any of them recalculates every suggestion and reloads the dashboard.

evidence.ref: docs/claims/calculations.md §2.4 Recalculation after a settings change

Other courses on the site pick up the new values at their next processing run.

Set the daily maximum

evidence.ref: docs/claims/calculations.md §1.1 Daily Max Amount is a cap

claims.text: On the [[Calculation]] tab, type the most water for one day in Daily Max Amount.
claims.note: Daily Max Amount, bound to the user-unit value (sa-settings-dlg.component.html:82-95; en-us.json:422). It sits on the Calculation tab (sa-settings-dlg.component.html:67-71).

claims.text: The box shows your number in your own units.
claims.note: The box holds the value in the user units, converted from the stored millimetres when the dialog opens (sa-settings-dlg.component.ts:354-365; sa-settings-dlg.component.html:84-94).

claims.text: It goes up to 15.
claims.note: The maximum is 15 (sa-settings-dlg.component.html:87), and the box refuses a keystroke that would take the value above its maximum (decimal-input.component.ts:126-129). Same ceiling as calculation-settings/2/2.

claims.text: If a digit does not appear, it would take the number above 15.
claims.note: The maximum is 15 (sa-settings-dlg.component.html:87), and the box refuses a keystroke that would take the value above its maximum (decimal-input.component.ts:126-129). Same ceiling as calculation-settings/2/2.

claims.text: The box refuses it.
claims.note: The maximum is 15 (sa-settings-dlg.component.html:87), and the box refuses a keystroke that would take the value above its maximum (decimal-input.component.ts:126-129). Same ceiling as calculation-settings/2/2.

claims.text: Every station that needs more than this gets the same suggestion, so a run of equal numbers means the cap.

evidence.ref: docs/claims/calculations.md §1.1 Daily Max Amount is a cap

claims.note: Reworded from calculation-settings/2/3: every station whose deficit exceeds the daily maximum lands on the same suggestion (SpatialAdjustService.cs:3041-3043), which is why runs of identical numbers appear.

claims.text: If you also changed Units of Measure in this visit, the amounts were saved rescaled by 25.4.
claims.note: Safety-critical correction kept (docs/text-corrections.md). The amounts are loaded in the user units at open (sa-settings-dlg.component.ts:354-365) and converted back with the unit selected at save time (:421-427). A unit change saved in the same visit therefore stores the old-unit figures as though they were already in the new unit, a factor of 25.4 either way, and also triggers a recalculation (:452-455). Reopening Settings shows the stored amounts in the new units. See preferences/2/6.

claims.text: Reopen [[Settings]] and check Daily Max Amount and Lynx Reference Amount before you push.
claims.note: Safety-critical correction kept (docs/text-corrections.md). A unit change saved in the same visit therefore stores the old-unit figures as though they were already in the new unit, a factor of 25.4 either way, and also triggers a recalculation (:452-455). Reopening Settings shows the stored amounts in the new units. See preferences/2/6.
